summary: An excerpt from a military fiction novel (labeled Book 15, part 49) in which Gunnery Sergeant Ray leads a Marine squad inserting by helicopter onto a desert drop point. The pilots question his order not to sweep the drop zone, and Ray monitors his squad over an open comm channel while viewing a tactical display. The squad moves through a narrow, one-way canyon, with Ray tense about the terrain and a lack of sentries, and his men take high-ground positions to cover the entrance.
one_line: Marine Gunny Ray leads a stealthy helicopter insertion into a desert box canyon, with his squad taking covering positions.
key_facts: Ray tells the pilots that the LT says surprise is essential to the operation and that they should not sweep the drop point.
Ray instructs the helicopter pilots to make their hover two klicks away and stay on alert.
The pilot responds with 'Whatever you say, Gunny, since the tape's running,' a reference to the craft's flight data recorder.
Ray drops his command helmet visor, and the geography becomes a greenish mottle sliced by gridlines.
Ray's squad is shown as seven orange blobs around a yellow sliver representing Ray on a computer simulation.
Ray switches from light enhanced night vision to infrared with a sub-vocalized command.
The choppers peel back to a safe recon position after the Marines are on the ground.
The squad sprints almost due east with profiles low.
The narrow canyon is described as a sandblasted gully of tight switchbacks and wind carved angles, and is one way in, one way out.
The canyon's sides are sheer and devoid of footholds, unlike the satellite-generated model.
Ray checks the canyon entrance with infrared for sentries and finds none.
Dhamers positions himself behind an outcropping to cover the entrance with his subby and remote detonated personnel mines.
Kluge deploys right and Hanfland deploys left, up the incline of New Mes bedrock.
Kluge and Hanfland match pace with the insertion team and can provide crossfire from the high ground.
